trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise); clock starts at discovery, the first day the breach is known or by reasonable diligence would have been known to any workforce member (164.404(a)(2))
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10 or more have out-of-date contact information)

obligation: HIPAA breach notice to HHS (500 or more)
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more (likely in this scenario: about 38,000 records)

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal

trigger: Breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving that state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents (or more than 500 residents of another state)

trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the hospital (inbound)
trigger: A business associate (EHR vendor, MSP, teleradiology group, and others) discovers a breach of the hospital's PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery (BAAs may set shorter)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information (includes medical history, treatment, and health insurance information) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach; notice under HIPAA is deemed compliant if the hospital timely provides a copy of that notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm the deemed-compliance path with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the hospital (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent that maintains personal information for the hospital has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following determination of the breach

trigger: Affected patients who reside outside Florida (the service area borders another state)
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: Voluntary (no statutory deadline for this hospital today)
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practical (day 0 to 1); supports the OFAC mitigating factor
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: County EMS and emergency management (diversion and status)
citation: Hospital emergency preparedness communication plan (42 CFR 485.625(c)(7)); county EMS diversion protocol
trigger: Decision to request ambulance diversion, or loss of capability that affects the community
deadline: At the time of the decision, and at each status change
notify: County EMS dispatch; county emergency management; regional receiving hospitals
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational duty under the hospital's own plan

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief of a covered incident; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-26. If finalized as proposed, critical access hospitals would be covered regardless of size; recheck when final

trigger: Breach of PHR identifiable health information
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - 16 CFR 318.1 excludes HIPAA covered entities

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Discovery of covered equipment in a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the hospital holds no federal contracts (Medicare participation is not a procurement contract)
